Design-Led

### Every Corner, a Frame

Guests, architects and photographers tell us the same thing: it is the small details. Hand-finished walls in warm, sun-washed tones. Curved, softly lit mirrors. Timber, rattan and linen. Bougainvillea climbing the facades, and a pool designed to be looked at as much as swum in.

Every inch of Nema was made with intention, which is why so many creators, photographers and stylish travellers come here to shoot. Bring your camera; the light does the rest.

“The property is beautiful, peaceful, and thoughtfully designed, with a unique atmosphere.”

A Day at Nema

### Slow Mornings, Golden Evenings

- 7:00

#### Sand before coffee

A short walk down the local pathway to Thomas Beach for an early swim on a mid-to-high tide.

- 9:00

#### Coffee, then focus

Brunch at Suka Espresso, three minutes on foot, then your sunlit work nook and 50 Mbps fibre Wi‑Fi.

- 14:00

#### The pool, or the surf

Float on the beach ledge of the 16m pool, or ride three minutes to the waves at Padang Padang.

- 17:30

#### Sunset on the cliffs

Live music at Single Fin, four minutes away, or the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple as the sun goes down.

- 22:00

#### A gentle hush

Back through the gate, Uluwatu's bustle falls away. Blackout curtains, cool linen, deep sleep.

Alone, Together

### Company, Without the Small Talk

Some days you want to be completely alone. Most days you simply want to be around people. With just a handful of studios around one pool, Nema lives in that gentle middle: a nod over morning coffee, a quiet chat on the sunbeds, and a door that closes whenever you want it to.

It is the thing solo travellers tell us they value most. A standalone villa can be beautiful and strangely isolating, with no one to ask for directions, a dinner tip or a driver. Here, our team is on hand day and night, and familiar faces are never far away.

#### Safe, without trying

Since we opened, the comment we hear most often from women travelling alone is simple: “I felt safe here.” Discreet 24/7 security and a 24-hour front desk are part of it. Just as important, you never need a scooter. The beach, YUKI, Kynd and dozens of cafes and restaurants are a short walk away, so you never need a scooter at night.
Our guide to solo travel in Uluwatu

The neighbourhood guide

Before You Arrive

### Essential Details

Answers to the questions we are asked most.

**Q: Are you walking distance to the beach and cafes in Uluwatu?**

Yes. Thomas Beach is a short walk down a local pathway, usually under ten minutes. Kynd Community (about 200 m), YUKI (about 400 m), Suka Espresso and Mood by Ours are all on foot, along with boutique shopping and some of Uluwatu's best restaurants. Bingin's cliffside cafes are a short ride away.

**Q: Is Nema suitable for solo female travellers?**

Absolutely. We prioritise your peace of mind so you can fully relax. Nema is a highly private sanctuary with discreet 24-hour on-site security and a 24-hour front desk. Our location also makes independent exploration effortless: you are a short, safe stroll from the local dining scene, so you never need a scooter at night.

**Q: Is Nema a good fit for independent travellers and remote workers?**

Yes. Nema is well suited to independent travellers, creatives and remote workers who want a premium, safe and sophisticated base. With 50 Mbps fibre Wi-Fi, a sunlit work nook in every studio and a relaxed communal pool, it is an easy place to focus, then switch off.

**Q: Can Nema be booked as a private yoga retreat accommodation in Uluwatu?**

Yes. Wellness instructors and corporate facilitators can reserve our entire 12-studio property to host an exclusive private retreat: 12 guests in private studios or up to 24 sharing, with a paved pool deck for practice and a covered common area for rainy days. Nema is venue-only, so the programme is yours; catering can be arranged on request. See the retreat page.

**Q: Will I feel isolated staying alone at Nema?**

No. With a handful of studios around one shared pool there is easy, low-key company when you want it, a private studio when you don't, and our team on site day and night for directions, dinner tips and drivers.

**Q: How much does a night at Nema Uluwatu cost?**

Studios are under US$150 per night even in peak season, less in low season, and last-minute rates are often available. Our seasonal rates are fair by design: we would rather be full than expensive. The best rate is always direct: message us on WhatsApp with your dates.

**Q: When is the best time to visit Uluwatu?**

The dry season, roughly April to October, brings the most sunshine, and July and August are the busiest months. April to June and September to October are quieter with excellent weather. November to March is the wet season: rain usually comes in short afternoon bursts, the pool stays warm, and rates are at their lowest apart from Christmas and New Year. Read our month-by-month guide.

**Q: Do I need a scooter to stay at Nema Uluwatu?**

No. Nema is in central Uluwatu, so Thomas Beach, Kynd Community (about 200 m), YUKI (about 400 m), Mood by Ours, Suka Espresso and many more restaurants and cafes are within walking distance. For longer trips, our front desk can arrange a driver through our transport partners, and scooter rental is available if you would like one.

**Q: What are the best restaurants near Nema, and do guests get a discount?**

Kynd Community is about 200 m away and YUKI about 400 m, with Mood by Ours, Suka Espresso, Osteria Luna and Tabu close by. Show your Nema keyring at partner restaurants and Parker Clothing for 10–20% off.

**Q: How do I get to Nema from the airport?**

Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS) is about 17 km from Nema, usually 40 to 60 minutes by car depending on traffic. Our transport partners can meet you at arrivals; ask us to arrange a driver when you book.

**Q: Is Nema a good place for photoshoots and content creators?**

Yes. Nema is design-led, and guests, architects and photographers often remark on the small details: hand-finished walls, curved mirrors, warm timber and bougainvillea climbing the facades. Every corner of the property works as a backdrop, which is why so many creators come to shoot. For commercial or brand shoots, contact us first.

**Q: Is Nema. Uluwatu a hotel or a villa?**

Nema. Uluwatu is a small boutique hotel, not a private villa or an apartment block: 12 private studios set around one shared 16m pool and garden, with a 24-hour front desk, daily housekeeping and on-site security. Each studio has its own queen bed, work nook and outdoor bathroom. Some booking sites list it as an aparthotel or serviced apartment because there is no restaurant on site.

# The Studios | Nema. Uluwatu, Bali
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/studios/
Summary: Private 25m² studios with queen beds, sunlit work nooks, 50 Mbps Wi-Fi and outdoor rain showers, a short walk from Thomas Beach, Uluwatu.

## The Studios

Twelve private studios, each one a quiet room of your own, a few minutes from Thomas Beach.

Inside Every Studio

### Designed for Rest, Made for Focus

Each of our 12 studios is a private, sunlit space with a dedicated work alcove, a queen-sized bed and a signature outdoor bathroom. The details are quiet but considered: linen with a high thread count, Sensatia Botanicals bath products made in Bali, and robes waiting on arrival.

Guests often single out the small things: curved, softly lit mirrors, hand-finished walls, built-in timber desks and the open sky above every shower. It is a studio made to be lived in, and photographed.

- Queen-sized bedMedium-firm mattress, premium linen and plush pillows.

- Sunlit work nookA dedicated desk alcove in every studio.

- 50 Mbps fibre Wi-FiFibre-optic connection for calls and creative work.

- Outdoor bathroomPrivate open-air rain shower. No bathtub.

- Sensatia BotanicalsShampoo, conditioner and body wash from the Bali-made botanical brand.

- Robes and towelsRobes waiting in your studio on arrival, with plush 550 gsm towels.

“This property was perfect, looks even better in person. The whole place is so well looked after.”

01

### A Desk in the Sun

Each studio has a dedicated, sunlit work alcove with a built-in timber desk. With 50 Mbps fibre-optic Wi-Fi throughout, it is a calm place to write, build or plan, then close the laptop and walk to the beach.

02

### The Outdoor Bathroom

Each studio has its own walled outdoor bathroom: a rain shower open to the sky, a stone basin and a curved, softly lit mirror. Shower under the tropical sun by day and the stars at night, in complete privacy.

03

### Step Outside

Studios open onto the garden and our 16m beach-ledge pool: swim, read on a lounger, or find easy company by the water. Discreet 24-hour on-site security keeps the whole property serene, day and night.

Studio Questions

### Good to Know

**Q: Do the studios at Nema have a bathtub?**

No. Each studio has a private outdoor bathroom with a rain shower, open to the tropical sun by day and the stars at night. There is no bathtub.

**Q: Can I work remotely from a studio at Nema Uluwatu?**

Yes. Every one of the 12 studios has a dedicated, sunlit work nook, and the property is connected with 50 Mbps fibre-optic Wi-Fi.

**Q: What bed do the studios have?**

Each studio has one premium queen-sized bed dressed in high-thread-count linen. Twin beds, cots and extra beds are not available, so each studio suits one or two guests.

**Q: Is breakfast included at Nema?**

Nema does not serve breakfast. Every studio has a kettle, local teas and a mini-fridge, and Suka Espresso, Kynd Community and Mood by Ours are a few minutes' walk for breakfast and brunch.

**Q: Are children welcome, and is there parking?**

Children of any age are welcome, though cots and extra beds are not available and each studio has one queen bed. Free private parking is available on site.

Reserve Direct

### Your Studio Is Waiting

Fair, seasonal rates, always best when you book direct. Message us on WhatsApp with your dates and we will confirm availability personally.

# Yoga Retreat Venue in Uluwatu, Bali | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/retreats/
Summary: Host your yoga or wellness retreat at Nema: 12 private studios, a paved pool deck for practice, covered space for rain and 10–20% partner dining.

Exclusive Property Reservation

## Your Retreat. Our Sanctuary.

A paved poolside deck made for practice, a private studio for every guest or couple, and the whole property reserved for your group.

For Yoga, Wellness & Team Retreats

### A Blank Canvas for the Retreat You Have in Mind

Made for yoga, health and wellness facilitators. Secure the entire 12-studio property to give your guests a private, premium sanctuary in the heart of Uluwatu.

Nema is a venue, not a package. We take care of the place: twelve calm studios, a sun-drenched pool deck, daily housekeeping and round-the-clock security. You bring the programme, the teachers and the people, and shape every day exactly as you want it.

01

### Practise by the Water

Roll out mats on our paved deck beside the 16m beach-ledge pool, a level, open space made for sunrise flows and golden-hour classes, with the garden, the sky and the sound of the water around you.

Our team clears the pool furniture before class to open up the deck. When the tropical rain arrives, move under cover to the common area, which can also be cleared, and carry on without missing a session.

02

### Rain-Ready Common Area

Step through the timber doors into a covered common area that opens onto the garden and pool. When an afternoon shower rolls in, practice simply moves under cover and carries on.

03

### A Private Compound

Twelve studios arranged around a single garden and pool create a natural sense of community, while every guest or couple keeps the privacy of their own studio. Tucked down a short lane off the main Uluwatu road, it is quiet inside and walkable outside.

04

### Rest That Restores

Each 25m² studio has a queen-sized bed in premium linen, blackout curtains, quiet split air-conditioning and its own terrace. Deep sleep is part of the programme, whether or not you planned it.

From Above

### The Paved Deck, Cleared for Practice

An overhead view of the 16m pool and the paved deck beside it. Our team moves the loungers before class, opening up the deck for your group's mats.

November to March

### The Off-Season Retreat

Our quietest months are the best time to bring a group to Nema. From November to March, Christmas and New Year aside, the whole property is easiest to reserve, rates are at their lowest of the year, and Uluwatu itself is calmer.

It is also Bali's wet season, which is gentler here than most people expect. Rain usually arrives in short afternoon bursts rather than all day. The pool stays warm for swimming, you can practise in the open between showers, and the covered common area keeps every session on schedule when the rain sets in.

Retreat Questions

### Essential Details

**Q: Can I reserve the entire Nema Uluwatu property for a yoga retreat?**

Yes. Retreat facilitators can reserve all 12 studios as an exclusive property reservation, so Nema is private to your group for the length of your retreat. Nema provides the venue; you run your own programme.

**Q: How many guests can a retreat at Nema accommodate?**

Nema has 12 private studios, each with one queen-sized bed. That suits 12 participants in private rooms, or up to 24 guests when participants share a studio.

**Q: Where can we practise yoga at Nema?**

Classes can be held on the paved deck beside the 16m pool, which our team clears of furniture for your sessions, or under cover in the common area when it rains.

**Q: Does Nema provide catering or run the retreat programme?**

Nema is a venue-only retreat property, so the programme is yours: you organise your own teachers and activities. Catering at Nema can be arranged on request, our partner restaurants offer Nema guests discounted group dinners, and cafes such as Suka Espresso are within walking distance.

**Q: When is the best time to host a retreat at Nema?**

November to March. These are our quietest months, when the whole property is easiest to reserve and rates are at their lowest. Rain usually comes in short afternoon bursts, the pool stays warm, and the covered common area keeps practice going whatever the weather.

**Q: How do I enquire about hosting a private retreat at Nema?**

Email nemauluwatu@gmail.com or message +62 813-3734-9684 on WhatsApp with your preferred dates, group size and the style of retreat you are planning.

**Q: What partner services can Nema arrange for a retreat?**

Nema works with many local partners: restaurants offering 10–20% off group dinners, transport for airport transfers and excursions, catering at Nema, fresh coconuts ordered in advance, extra seating and custom co-branded yoga mats. Our team can also help design a local itinerary within your budget, scooter rental is available, and drinks can be bought on site.

# Where to Stay in Uluwatu: The Neighbourhood | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/uluwatu/
Summary: Walk to Thomas Beach, Kynd and YUKI from Nema in central Uluwatu. Distances, top restaurants, sunsets, day clubs and 10–20% restaurant discounts.

Uluwatu · Bingin · Padang Padang

## Perfectly Positioned

In the heart of Uluwatu, tucked down a quiet lane. The beach, the cafes and the cliffs are all within minutes.

The Neighbourhood

### The Best of Both Worlds

Nema sits in the heart of Uluwatu, just off the main road down a short lane. Step through the gate and the noise falls away; step back out and Uluwatu's cafes, boutiques and spas are all around you.

Walk to Thomas Beach for a morning swim. Book a reformer class, then brunch at Suka Espresso. Spend the afternoon at a cliffside day club, and watch the sun drop into the ocean from Single Fin before dinner at YUKI.

Distances From Nema

### Everything Within Minutes

- Short walkThomas BeachWhite sand and turquoise water, down a local pathway

- 3 min walkSuka EspressoA local favourite for coffee and brunch

- 5 min walkSpring Spa UluwatuMassage, manicures and treatments

- 3 min ridePadang Padang BeachWorld-class surf, or a 20-minute walk

- 4 min rideSingle Fin, Blue PointLive music and clifftop sunsets

- 5–7 min rideUluwatu TempleThe nightly Kecak fire dance

- Short rideBinginThe neighbouring surf village and beach

- 17 kmNgurah Rai AirportBali's international airport

Getting Here

### Getting to Nema

Bali's Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS) is about 17 km from Nema, 40 to 60 minutes by car depending on traffic. Our transport partners can meet you at arrivals.

- 3h 45mFrom PerthDirect, and the same time zone as Bali: no jet lag.

- About 6hFrom Sydney, Melbourne & BrisbaneDirect flights daily. Bali is only 2–3 hours behind.

- About 17hFrom LondonOne stop. Bali is 7–8 hours ahead.

- 16–18hFrom Frankfurt, Zurich & AmsterdamOne stop. Bali is 6–7 hours ahead.

- About 9hFrom DubaiDirect. Bali is 4 hours ahead.

- 20h+From Los AngelesOne stop. Bali is 15–16 hours ahead.

- About 2h 40mFrom SingaporeDirect, and the main hub for flights from Europe.

- On arrivalVisa & levyVisa on Arrival for most visitors, about IDR 500,000 for 30 days, plus the IDR 150,000 Bali tourist levy, paid online or on arrival.

Flight times are approximate. Entry rules are correct as of October 2026; check the latest requirements before you travel.

01

### The Best of Uluwatu's Food Scene

Nema sits at the heart of Uluwatu's food scene. Some of the area's best restaurants are a few minutes' walk from the gate, and your Nema keyring takes 10–20% off at our partners.

- Kynd CommunityAbout 200m. Famous for its photogenic smoothie bowls and brunch.

- YUKIAbout 400m. Modern Japanese izakaya, sushi and cocktails; a date-night favourite.

- Mood by OursA short walk on Jl. Labuansait. Farm-to-table cafe and organic market.

- Suka EspressoAbout a 3-minute walk. The local favourite for coffee and a long brunch.

- Osteria LunaCoastal Italian on the Padang Padang strip, from the team behind YUKI.

- TabuSleek and atmospheric, made for a long dinner.

02

### Sunsets & Day Clubs

Uluwatu faces west, so every evening ends with the sun dropping into the Indian Ocean. Start the day with a swim at Thomas Beach, a short walk away, then choose your cliff.

- Single FinAbout 4 minutes by ride. Live music above the Uluwatu break.

- OneEightyThe glass-bottom infinity pool hanging over the cliffs. More champagne than shots.

- Ulu Cliffhouse & El KabronClifftop pools, long lunches and sunset cocktails.

- Sundays Beach ClubA full beach day on white sand at the bottom of the cliffs.

- SavayaUluwatu's headline clifftop club for big DJ nights.

03

### Move & Unwind

Mornings in Uluwatu belong to reformer Pilates, surf lessons and slow yoga; afternoons to massages and boutique shopping.

- Bluvana StudioClose by. Intimate reformer Pilates with small classes.

- Reform Pilates & Studio FondueTwo of the area's most popular reformer studios.

- Spring Spa UluwatuAbout a 5-minute walk, for massages and manicures.

- Padang PadangAbout 3 minutes by ride, for surf and a little Eat Pray Love nostalgia.

- Learn to surfThomas Beach has a friendly learner wave a short walk away. Read our surf guide.

- Parker ClothingBoutique shopping nearby. Nema guests save 10–20% with their keyring.

04

### For Solo Travellers

We prioritise your peace of mind so you can fully relax. Nema has discreet 24-hour on-site security and a 24-hour front desk, and the local dining scene is a short, safe stroll away, so you never need to ride a scooter at night. It is the thing women travelling alone tell us most: they feel safe here.

“As we were two girls travelling we felt safe in the villa as there was overnight security and reception staff every day.”

Nina, Australia · Booking.com

Local Questions

### Essential Details

**Q: How far is Nema Uluwatu from Thomas Beach?**

Thomas Beach is a short walk from Nema down a local pathway, typically under ten minutes on foot.

**Q: Where are the best places to eat and drink near Nema Uluwatu?**

Suka Espresso is about a three-minute walk for coffee and brunch, and Kynd Community is about 200 m away. For dinner, YUKI and Tabu are date-night favourites where Nema guests save 10–20% with their keyring. For sunset, Single Fin is about four minutes away by ride, with cliffside spots like OneEighty, Ulu Cliffhouse and El Kabron along the coast.

**Q: How far is Nema from Padang Padang, Single Fin and Uluwatu Temple?**

Padang Padang Beach is about 3 minutes by car or scooter, or a 20-minute walk. Single Fin at Blue Point is about 4 minutes by car, and Uluwatu Temple, with its nightly Kecak fire dance, is 5 to 7 minutes by car. Ngurah Rai International Airport is about 17 km away.

**Q: Is Uluwatu safe for solo female travellers staying at Nema?**

Uluwatu is generally relaxed and welcoming for women travelling alone, and many of our guests are on a first solo trip. Nema is a highly private sanctuary with discreet 24-hour on-site security and a 24-hour front desk, just off the main Uluwatu road, so cafes and restaurants are a short, safe stroll away and you never need a scooter at night.

**Q: How do I get from the airport to Nema Uluwatu?**

Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS) is about 17 km from Nema, usually 40 to 60 minutes by car depending on traffic. Our transport partners can meet you at arrivals; ask us to arrange a driver when you book.

**Q: How long is the flight to Bali from Australia, the UK and Europe?**

Perth to Bali is about 3 hours 45 minutes direct, and Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane about 6 hours direct. From London it is about 17 hours with one stop; from Frankfurt, Zurich or Amsterdam 16 to 18 hours with one stop; from Dubai about 9 hours direct. Flight times are approximate.

**Q: Do I need a visa for Bali?**

Most visitors from Australia, the UK, EU countries, Switzerland and the US use a Visa on Arrival, or the online e-VoA: about IDR 500,000 for 30 days, extendable once. Bali also charges a tourist levy of IDR 150,000 per visitor, payable online before you fly or on arrival. These details are correct as of October 2026, but rules change, so check before you travel.

**Q: What time zone is Bali in?**

Bali is on Central Indonesian Time (UTC+8), the same as Perth. It is two to three hours behind Sydney and Melbourne, seven to eight hours ahead of London and six to seven hours ahead of Central Europe, so jet lag is minimal for Australian visitors.

# Solo Female Travel in Uluwatu: Safety & Stays | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/solo-female-travel-uluwatu/
Summary: Is Uluwatu safe for solo female travellers? Where to stay, getting around without a scooter, and how to enjoy Uluwatu entirely on your own.

Solo Travel

## Solo Female Travel in Uluwatu: A Local Guide

Where to stay, how to get around, and how to enjoy Uluwatu entirely on your own terms.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 6 min read

Uluwatu is one of Bali's easiest places to travel alone. It is slower than Canggu, more beautiful than almost anywhere on the island, and full of cafes, yoga studios and beaches where nobody looks twice at a woman on her own. Here is what we tell our solo guests before they arrive.

### Is Uluwatu safe for women travelling alone?

In our experience, yes. Uluwatu is relaxed and friendly, and solo women are a normal part of its cafe and surf scene. Most of the stress solo travellers describe in Bali has little to do with people and a lot to do with logistics: dark roads, long scooter rides, and accommodation that is beautiful on Instagram but isolated in real life.

So the two decisions that matter most are where you sleep and how you get home in the evening. Get those right and the rest of the trip takes care of itself.

Since we opened, the comment we hear most from women travelling alone is that they feel safe at Nema. Discreet 24/7 security and a 24-hour front desk are part of it. The other part is simple: you never need to scoot. Kynd Community is about 200m away, YUKI about 400m, and the beach and dozens of restaurants are on foot, so you are never on a scooter after dark.

“As we were two girls travelling we felt safe in the villa as there was overnight security and reception staff every day.”

Nina, Australia · Booking.com

### Where to stay

Uluwatu is spread out across the Bukit Peninsula, and many villas sit down long, unlit lanes. For a solo trip we suggest a checklist like this:

- 24-hour security and staff on site. Someone awake at the front desk at 2am is worth more than any amenity.

- A walkable location. Being able to walk to dinner and back changes how free you feel in the evening.

- A small property. Fewer rooms mean staff know who belongs there, and other guests become familiar faces.

- Somewhere sociable, but private. A shared pool for easy conversation; a room that is entirely yours when you want quiet.

That is exactly why Nema works so well for solo guests. It has 12 private studios around a 16m pool in central Uluwatu, tucked down a short lane off the main Uluwatu road. There is discreet 24-hour on-site security and a 24-hour front desk, and Suka Espresso is a three-minute walk away.

#### Villa or small hotel?

A private villa looks like the dream on Instagram. Travelling alone, it can be strangely isolating: a big, quiet space, nobody to ask which beach is best today, and no one to call a driver at midnight. A small boutique property gives you the same privacy behind your own door, with people around when you want them.

At Nema we call it alone, together. With only twelve studios, you start recognising faces within a day. A nod over coffee, a quiet chat on the sunbeds, and never any pressure to make conversation. Some guests end up swapping dinner tips or heading to sunset together; others never say more than good morning, and that is fine too.

And because our rates follow the seasons, a boutique stay here often costs less than a standalone villa nearby. Show your Nema keyring at partner venues like YUKI, Kynd and Tabu for 10–20% off, too.

### Getting around without stress

Many visitors assume they need a scooter in Uluwatu. If you are not an experienced rider, we would gently suggest you don't: the roads are steep, busy and unlit in places, and Indonesia requires a valid licence that covers motorbikes. Instead:

- Walk wherever you can. From central Uluwatu, Thomas Beach, cafes, spas and restaurants are all on foot. Our guide to Uluwatu without a scooter covers it in detail.

- Use Grab or Gojek, the main ride-hailing apps in Bali, for longer trips. You see the driver, the plate and the route before you get in.

- Ask the front desk to help arrange a trusted driver for airport runs or day trips.

### Days and nights on your own

Uluwatu is made for the kind of solo day that never feels lonely: an early swim at Thomas Beach, a reformer class, a long brunch, an afternoon by the pool, and sunset on the cliffs.

- Mornings: Thomas Beach is a short walk away and quiet early in the day.

- Move: reformer Pilates is a big part of life here. Bluvana Studio, close by, keeps classes small, and Reform Pilates and Studio Fondue are popular with regulars.

- Brunch: Suka Espresso is three minutes on foot and an easy place to sit alone for hours; Kynd Community is known for its photogenic smoothie bowls.

- Afternoons: book a sunbed at a cliffside day club like OneEighty or Ulu Cliffhouse, where plenty of people come solo.

- Sunset: Single Fin at Blue Point, around four minutes by ride, has live music and a crowd that is easy to be part of on your own.

- Culture: the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset is unforgettable, and a short ride from Nema.

### Small habits that help

- Keep your phone charged and offline maps downloaded.

- Share your plans with someone at home, or with the front desk, if you are heading out late.

- Book a ride home before the end of the night rather than looking for one on the street.

- Keep an eye on your drink, as you would anywhere.

- Carry a little cash; some warungs and smaller shops prefer it.

Most of all, enjoy it. Travelling alone in Uluwatu is one of the great slow pleasures of Bali.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: Is Uluwatu safe for solo female travellers?**

Uluwatu is generally considered a relaxed and welcoming place for women travelling alone, and many of our guests are on their first solo trip. As anywhere, the biggest factors are where you stay and how you get around at night: choose accommodation with 24-hour security and somewhere walkable to cafes and restaurants, and use registered ride-hailing apps rather than unofficial lifts.

**Q: Where should a solo female traveller stay in Uluwatu?**

Look for a small property with on-site security and staff, close to cafes and restaurants so you are not relying on a scooter after dark. Nema. Uluwatu is a 12-studio boutique property in central Uluwatu with discreet 24-hour security and a 24-hour front desk, a short walk from Thomas Beach and a three-minute walk from Suka Espresso.

**Q: Do I need a scooter to stay in Uluwatu alone?**

Not if you stay centrally. From central Uluwatu you can walk to Thomas Beach, cafes, spas and restaurants, and use Grab or Gojek for longer trips such as Uluwatu Temple or Bingin.

**Q: Is Uluwatu good for meeting other travellers?**

Yes. Uluwatu has a sociable cafe, Pilates and surf culture. At a small property like Nema, with only 12 studios around one pool, it is easy to have a quiet chat with other guests without any pressure to socialise, and you always have a private studio to retreat to.

**Q: Is a private villa or a small hotel better for solo travel in Uluwatu?**

Many solo travellers find a standalone villa isolating, with no staff on hand for directions, tips or drivers. A small boutique property such as Nema offers the same privacy in your own studio, with a 24-hour front desk and familiar faces around the pool, often at a lower price than a private villa.

# Uluwatu Without a Scooter: What You Can Walk To | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/uluwatu-without-a-scooter/
Summary: Can you enjoy Uluwatu without a scooter? Yes, if you stay central. What you can walk to from Nema, when to use Grab or Gojek, and travel times.

Getting Around

## Uluwatu Without a Scooter: What You Can Walk To

Stay central, walk to the beach and the cafes, and save rides for the sunsets.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 5 min read

Scooters are part of the Bali postcard, but they are not compulsory. If you stay in the right part of Uluwatu, you can spend a week here on foot, with the occasional app ride, and never miss a sunset. This is how.

### Why skip the scooter?

Uluwatu's roads are steep, winding and busy, and some stretches are unlit at night. Indonesia also requires a valid licence that covers motorbikes, and many travel insurance policies will not cover you without one. For experienced riders, a scooter is freedom. For everyone else, it is the most common way a holiday goes wrong.

### Stay central, not remote

Uluwatu is not one village; it is a collection of clifftop areas spread across the Bukit Peninsula. Many beautiful villas are a long way from anything, which is wonderful until you want dinner. The single best decision for a scooter-free trip is to stay in central Uluwatu, on or just off the main Uluwatu road, where cafes, spas and restaurants are on your doorstep.

Nema is right there: tucked down a short lane off the main road, so it is quiet inside but walkable outside.

### What you can walk to from Nema

Distances from Nema. Uluwatu

| Place | From Nema | Why go

| Thomas Beach | Short walk | Down a local pathway to white sand and turquoise water.

| Suka Espresso | 3 min walk | Coffee, acai bowls and brunch.

| Spring Spa Uluwatu | 5 min walk | Massage, manicures and treatments.

| Kynd Community | Walkable | Smoothie bowls and brunch on Jl. Labuansait.

| Bluvana Studio | Nearby | Small-group reformer Pilates.

| Padang Padang Beach | 20 min walk | Or about 3 minutes by ride.

| Single Fin, Blue Point | 4 min ride | Clifftop sunsets and live music.

| Uluwatu Temple | 5–7 min ride | Sunset Kecak fire dance.

| Ngurah Rai Airport | 17 km | Allow extra time for traffic.

For more on each place, see our neighbourhood guide.

### When to take a ride

For anything beyond walking distance, you have four easy options:

- Grab or Gojek. Bali's main ride-hailing apps, available as car or motorbike-taxi rides. You see the price and the driver before you book.

- A local driver. In some areas, local transport rules limit where app drivers can pick up. If that happens, our front desk can help arrange a trusted local driver.

- A day driver. For a day of temples and beaches, hiring a car and driver for the day is relaxed and good value. Nema works with local transport partners and can arrange it for you.

- A scooter, if you want one. Experienced riders can rent a scooter through Nema; just ask the front desk.

Ngurah Rai International Airport is about 17 km away. Distance is not the issue; traffic is. Allow extra time, especially in the late afternoon.

### A day in Uluwatu on foot

- 7:00 Walk the local pathway down to Thomas Beach for an early swim.

- 9:00 Brunch at Suka Espresso, three minutes from the gate.

- 11:00 Back to your studio's sunlit work nook, or straight to the pool.

- 16:00 A massage at Spring Spa Uluwatu, five minutes on foot.

- 18:00 A short ride to Single Fin for sunset, or the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple.

- 20:30 Dinner nearby, then a short walk home.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: Can you get around Uluwatu without a scooter?**

Yes, if you stay centrally. From central Uluwatu you can walk to Thomas Beach, cafes, spas and restaurants, and use Grab, Gojek or a driver for longer trips to places like Uluwatu Temple, Bingin or the airport.

**Q: What can you walk to from Nema Uluwatu?**

Thomas Beach is a short walk down a local pathway. Suka Espresso is about three minutes on foot, Spring Spa Uluwatu about five, and Padang Padang Beach about twenty. Kynd Community is on the same main road.

**Q: Do Grab and Gojek work in Uluwatu?**

Grab and Gojek are the main ride-hailing apps in Bali and are widely used around Uluwatu. In some areas local transport rules limit where app drivers can pick up, so if a pickup is difficult, ask your accommodation to arrange a local driver.

**Q: How far is Nema Uluwatu from the airport?**

Ngurah Rai International Airport is about 17 km from Nema. Journey times vary a lot with traffic, so allow extra time, particularly in the late afternoon.

# How to Choose a Bali Retreat Venue | Nema. Uluwatu
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/bali-retreat-venue-checklist/
Summary: Planning a yoga or wellness retreat in Bali? A practical venue checklist: exclusive use, rooms, practice space, rain backup, meals and transfers.

For Facilitators

## How to Choose a Bali Retreat Venue: A Checklist

Twelve things to check before you sign, from rain backup to room configuration.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 6 min read

The venue is the single biggest decision in planning a retreat. It sets your price, your participants' experience and how much you will be firefighting on the day. Here is the checklist we would use, from the other side of the reception desk.

### The checklist

-

#### Exclusive use

Can you reserve the whole property? Sharing a venue with other guests changes the energy of a retreat completely, and makes quiet practice and group moments harder.

-

#### Room configuration

Count beds, not rooms. Decide whether participants get private rooms or share, because that drives your pricing. Twelve rooms with one queen bed each, for example, suit 12 people in private rooms or up to 24 sharing.

-

#### Practice space

Where will you actually teach? Look at the surface, shade, noise and how many mats it fits. Ask for photos taken at the time of day you plan to teach.

-

#### Rain backup

Bali's wet season runs roughly from November to March. A covered area for practice is non-negotiable if your dates fall in those months.

-

#### Meals

Is catering included, optional or not offered? If not offered, are there good cafes within walking distance, and can you bring in your own caterer or private chef?

-

#### Location and walkability

A walkable venue gives participants free time without you organising transport for every outing. It also makes your marketing easier: beach, cafes and sunsets are part of the offer.

-

#### Airport transfers

Check the distance to Ngurah Rai Airport and plan group transfers. Traffic, not distance, decides how long it takes.

-

#### Sleep quality

Air-conditioning, blackout curtains and quiet at night matter more than anything on a retreat. Tired participants do not have transformative weeks.

-

#### Wi-Fi and work space

Even on a digital-detox retreat, you need to run your business. Ask for actual speeds.

-

#### Security and staff

Is there 24-hour security and a front desk? It reassures participants, especially women travelling alone.

-

#### Daily housekeeping

Clean rooms every day lift the whole experience and are one less thing for you to manage.

-

#### What is included, in writing

Get a clear list of what the venue provides and what you bring, so you can price your retreat with confidence.

### Venue-only or all-inclusive?

All-inclusive retreat centres handle food, activities and sometimes even marketing. That is convenient, but you are fitting your retreat into their format. A venue-only property gives you the space and the hospitality, and leaves the programme entirely to you: your teachers, your food philosophy, your schedule and your price.

For independent facilitators building a recognisable retreat brand, venue-only is often the better fit.

### How Nema measures up

Nema. Uluwatu is a venue-only retreat property in central Uluwatu:

- Exclusive use of all 12 private studios.

- 12 to 24 guests: one queen bed per studio, private or shared.

- Practice on the pool deck around the 16m pool, or under cover in the common area when it rains.

- Catering on request: catering at Nema can be arranged, partner restaurants offer discounted group dinners, and Suka Espresso is a short walk away.

- Air-conditioning, blackout curtains, 50 Mbps fibre Wi-Fi, daily housekeeping, 24-hour front desk and security.

- A short walk from Thomas Beach; about 17 km from the airport.

See the full details on our retreat page.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: What should I look for in a Bali retreat venue?**

Check that you can have exclusive use of the property, that the room configuration fits your group and pricing, that there is a practice space with a covered backup for rain, how meals will work, how far the venue is from the airport, and what is and is not included.

**Q: Is it better to book a venue-only retreat property or an all-inclusive retreat centre?**

A venue-only property gives you full control over your programme, teachers, food and pricing, and usually more character and privacy. An all-inclusive centre does more for you but leaves less room to shape the experience. Many independent facilitators prefer venue-only.

**Q: When is the rainy season in Bali?**

Bali's wet season generally runs from around November to March, with heavy but often short tropical showers. If you plan a retreat in those months, make sure your venue has a covered space for practice.

**Q: How many people can Nema Uluwatu host for a retreat?**

Nema has 12 private studios, each with one queen-sized bed, which suits 12 participants in private rooms or up to 24 guests sharing. Practice takes place on the paved pool deck or under cover in the common area when it rains. Nema is venue-only, so the programme is yours; catering at Nema can be arranged on request.

Send us your dates and group size. We reply personally.

# Uluwatu for Couples: Stay, Eat & Sunsets | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/uluwatu-for-couples/
Summary: A romantic guide to Uluwatu for couples: where to stay, date-night restaurants, clifftop sunsets, day clubs and a perfect day for two.

For Two

## Uluwatu for Couples: A Slow, Romantic Guide

Date nights, clifftop sunsets and slow mornings, from a quiet studio near Thomas Beach.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 6 min read

Uluwatu is Bali at its most cinematic: limestone cliffs, turquoise water and a sunset every single evening. It is also slower and calmer than the island's busier towns, which makes it perfect for two. Here is how we would spend a few days here together.

### Why Uluwatu for two

Uluwatu sits on the Bukit Peninsula at Bali's southern tip. The coast faces west, so every day ends with the sun dropping into the Indian Ocean. Between the beaches, the clifftop bars and an excellent restaurant scene, there is enough to fill a week without ever feeling rushed.

### Where to stay

Large resorts can feel anonymous; standalone villas can feel remote. For couples we suggest something in between: a small boutique hotel with your own private room, a beautiful shared pool, and staff who can book a table or a driver in minutes.

Nema has a handful of private studios around a 16m pool in central Uluwatu. Each studio has a queen bed with premium linen, blackout curtains for lazy mornings, its own balcony and a private outdoor rain shower. Thomas Beach is a short walk away, and rates are under US$150 a night even in peak season, which leaves more for long dinners.

“Absolutely stunning. A beautiful little sanctuary, such a relaxed vibe with complete attention to detail.”

Kirran, Australia · Booking.com

### Date nights

- YUKI: a date-night favourite close to Nema. Show your Nema keyring for a guest discount.

- Tabu: sleek and atmospheric, made for a long dinner. Also a Nema partner.

- Mana Uluwatu: cliffside dining above the surf.

- El Kabron: a clifftop classic for dinner as the sun goes down.

### Sunsets and day clubs

Spend an afternoon at a cliffside day club: OneEighty's glass-bottom pool, Ulu Cliffhouse, or Sundays Beach Club on the sand below the cliffs. Then stay for sunset, or move to Single Fin for live music. Our full guide to the best sunset spots in Uluwatu has more.

### A perfect day for two

- 7:30 A swim at Thomas Beach before the day warms up.

- 9:30 A reformer class together at Bluvana Studio, close by, then brunch at Suka Espresso.

- 13:00 Back to the pool, or side-by-side massages at Spring Spa, five minutes' walk away.

- 16:00 Sunbeds at a cliffside day club.

- 18:00 Sunset, then the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple.

- 20:00 Dinner at YUKI or Tabu, and a short ride home to a quiet studio.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: Is Uluwatu good for couples?**

Yes. Uluwatu is one of the most romantic parts of Bali: dramatic cliffs, white-sand beaches, west-facing sunsets over the Indian Ocean, and a dining scene built for long dinners. It is calmer than Canggu or Seminyak, which suits couples who want to slow down together.

**Q: Where should couples stay in Uluwatu?**

Choose somewhere private but walkable. A small boutique hotel gives you your own quiet studio with staff on hand for bookings and drivers. Nema. Uluwatu has a handful of private studios around one pool in central Uluwatu, a short walk from Thomas Beach, at under US$150 a night even in peak season.

**Q: What are the best date-night restaurants in Uluwatu?**

YUKI and Tabu are popular date-night choices close to Nema, and Nema guests save 10–20% at both with their keyring. Mana Uluwatu offers cliffside dining above the surf, and El Kabron is a favourite for a sunset dinner.

**Q: What is the most romantic thing to do in Uluwatu?**

Watch the sunset together. Single Fin, OneEighty, Ulu Cliffhouse and El Kabron all sit on the cliffs facing west, and the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset is unforgettable.

# The Best Sunset Spots in Uluwatu, Bali | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/best-sunset-spots-uluwatu/
Summary: Where to watch the sunset in Uluwatu: the Kecak fire dance, Single Fin, OneEighty, Ulu Cliffhouse, El Kabron and quiet beaches, plus timing tips.

Golden Hour

## The Best Sunset Spots in Uluwatu

From the Kecak fire dance to clifftop cocktails: where to be when the sun goes down.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 5 min read

Uluwatu's coastline faces west, which means one thing: the sun sets over the Indian Ocean every single evening. Where you watch it from is one of the best decisions you will make all day. These are our favourites.

### Seven places to watch the sunset

-

#### Uluwatu Temple and the Kecak fire dance

A clifftop temple about 70 metres above the ocean, and a sunset performance of the Kecak fire dance in its amphitheatre. Arrive in the late afternoon to walk the grounds first. Keep sunglasses and phones close: the resident monkeys are famous for snatching them. About 5 to 7 minutes from Nema.

-

#### Single Fin

The original Uluwatu sunset bar, perched above the surf break with live music and a buzzing, easy crowd. Easy to enjoy solo or as a couple. About 4 minutes by ride.

-

#### OneEighty

A glass-bottom infinity pool hanging off the cliffs, and the most dramatic sunset photos in Uluwatu. More champagne than shots.

-

#### Ulu Cliffhouse

A clifftop pool club with low-key DJs, made for a long afternoon that slides into sunset.

-

#### El Kabron

A Spanish-inspired clifftop restaurant and a classic spot for a sunset dinner.

-

#### Sundays Beach Club

For sunset with your toes in the sand, on a white beach at the bottom of the cliffs. Expect a minimum spend.

-

#### A quiet beach

Skip the crowds and walk down to a west-facing beach with a cold coconut. Thomas Beach is a short walk from Nema.

### Sunset tips

- Timing: sunset falls between about 6pm and 6:45pm, depending on the month. Arrive 45 to 60 minutes early.

- Season: the dry season, roughly April to October, tends to bring the clearest skies.

- Getting there: book a Grab or Gojek before you go and your ride home before it gets dark. Our front desk can arrange a driver.

- Minimum spends: many beach and day clubs have one in peak season, so check before you go.

Staying at Nema puts you minutes from most of these, with a short walk to the beach. Show your Nema keyring at partner venues for guest discounts.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: Where is the best place to watch the sunset in Uluwatu?**

Popular choices include the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple, Single Fin above the Uluwatu surf break, the glass-bottom pool at OneEighty, Ulu Cliffhouse and El Kabron on the cliffs, and Sundays Beach Club on the sand. For something quieter, head to a west-facing beach.

**Q: What time is sunset in Uluwatu?**

Because Bali is close to the equator, sunset falls between about 6pm and 6:45pm, depending on the month. Arrive 45 to 60 minutes early for the best seats, especially at popular clifftop venues and Uluwatu Temple.

**Q: When does the Kecak dance at Uluwatu Temple start?**

The Kecak fire dance is performed every evening at the temple's clifftop amphitheatre, timed around sunset (the performance starts at about 6pm). It is very popular, so arrive early and expect crowds.

**Q: How far are the sunset spots from Nema Uluwatu?**

Single Fin is about four minutes by ride and Uluwatu Temple five to seven minutes. Most clifftop venues are a short drive along the coast.

# Uluwatu vs Canggu: Where to Stay in Bali | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/uluwatu-vs-canggu/
Summary: Uluwatu or Canggu? An honest comparison for solo travellers and couples: scenery, beaches, nightlife, traffic, walkability and where to stay.

Where to Stay

## Uluwatu vs Canggu: Which Is Right for You?

Cliffs or rice fields, calm or buzz? An honest comparison of Bali's two favourite bases.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 5 min read

Uluwatu and Canggu are Bali's two favourite bases for independent travellers, and they could hardly be more different. One is cliffs, coves and sunsets; the other is cafes, crowds and buzz. Here is an honest comparison, from people who love both.

### At a glance

Uluwatu compared with Canggu

| | Uluwatu | Canggu

| Feel | Calm, scenic, upscale | Busy, social, buzzy

| Scenery | Limestone cliffs, turquoise coves | Black-sand beaches, rice fields

| Sunsets | Clifftop, over the ocean | On the beach

| Food and drink | Destination restaurants, cliff clubs | Dense cafe and bar scene

| Nightlife | Sunset sessions, big club nights | Every night of the week

| Getting around | Spread out; stay central to walk | Flat, but heavy traffic

| Best for | Slowing down, couples, retreats | Meeting people, long stays

### Choose Canggu if…

You want energy. Canggu has one of the densest cafe, coworking and bar scenes in Asia, and it is easy to meet people every night of the week. The trade-off is traffic, noise and a beach that is better for surfing than swimming.

### Choose Uluwatu if…

You want to slow down. Uluwatu's beaches are some of Bali's most beautiful, its sunsets are watched from clifftops, and its restaurants and day clubs are made for long afternoons. It is calmer and feels more grown-up.

The one thing to get right is where you stay. Uluwatu is spread out, and a remote villa can mean relying on rides for everything. Stay in central Uluwatu and you can walk to the beach, cafes, spas and restaurants, as we explain in Uluwatu without a scooter.

### Can't decide? Do both

Plenty of travellers split their trip: a few social days in Canggu, then a slower week in Uluwatu to finish. End in Uluwatu, and you will fly home properly rested.

### Staying at Nema

Nema is a small boutique hotel in central Uluwatu, a short walk from Thomas Beach, with private studios around one pool, 24-hour staff and rates under US$150 a night even in peak season. You get the calm of Uluwatu with the walkability people usually associate with Canggu.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: Is Uluwatu or Canggu better?**

It depends on your trip. Canggu is flatter, busier and more social, with a dense cafe and nightlife scene. Uluwatu is calmer and more scenic, with cliffs, clearer water, clifftop sunsets and a more upscale feel. Many travellers who want to relax choose Uluwatu.

**Q: Is Uluwatu or Canggu better for solo female travellers?**

Both are popular with solo women. Canggu makes it easier to meet people; Uluwatu is quieter and more relaxing. In Uluwatu, staying centrally matters: in central Uluwatu you can walk to the beach, cafes and spas, and a small boutique property with 24-hour staff makes evenings easy.

**Q: Is Uluwatu or Canggu better for couples?**

Uluwatu is often preferred by couples for its dramatic scenery, west-facing sunsets and romantic clifftop restaurants. Canggu suits couples who want a livelier scene.

**Q: How far is Uluwatu from the airport compared with Canggu?**

Both are a similar distance from Ngurah Rai International Airport. Nema is about 17 km away; travel time depends heavily on traffic, so allow extra time at busy hours.

# Best Time to Visit Uluwatu, Bali: Month by Month | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/best-time-to-visit-uluwatu/
Summary: When to visit Uluwatu, Bali: dry season, shoulder months, peak August and the truth about the rainy season, with the quietest, best-value months.

When to Go

## The Best Time to Visit Uluwatu, Month by Month

Dry season, shoulder months, and the truth about the rain.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 6 min read

Uluwatu has two seasons, dry and wet, and both are better than their reputation. The secret is that the best weeks are usually not the ones everyone books. Here is how the year really feels on the Bukit Peninsula.

### The year at a glance

Uluwatu weather and crowds by month

| Months | Season | What to expect

| January – March | Wet season | Quietest and best value. Warm, green and lush, with short afternoon downpours. Nyepi falls in March.

| April | Shoulder | The rain eases and the island is at its greenest. Busy over Easter, quiet otherwise. One of our favourite months.

| May – June | Dry season | Sunny, settled weather before the July and August peak. Ideal for beaches and sunsets.

| July – August | Peak season | The busiest months, with the highest prices across Bali. August is our busiest month: book well ahead.

| September – October | Dry season | Still dry and sunny as the peak-season crowds thin out. Excellent value for the weather.

| November – December | Wet season begins | Showers return and the island quietens, until the Christmas and New Year rush.

### The sweet spot: April to June, September to October

If you can choose your dates, choose these. The dry season brings sunshine and consistent surf, but the shoulder months either side of the July and August peak are when Uluwatu is at its best: beaches without crowds, easy restaurant bookings, and lower prices than July and August.

April is special. The rain has eased, the island is lush and green after the wet season, and outside Easter week most travellers have not arrived yet. At Nema our rates are seasonal, so the shoulder months are noticeably better value than the peak, while still under US$150 a night.

### Peak season

July and August are the European summer holidays, Australia’s winter school break falls in July, and this is the busiest time of year across Bali. The weather is reliably beautiful, but beaches, day clubs and roads are at their fullest and prices are at their highest. August is our busiest month, so book early if these are your dates.

### Flying in from Australia, the UK and Europe

- From Australia: Perth is under four hours away and in the same time zone; the east coast is about six hours with almost no jet lag. Fares jump in the school holidays, around April, July, late September to early October and from mid-December. May, June and October give you dry-season weather at everyday prices.

- From the UK: about 17 hours with one stop. Avoid Christmas, Easter and the late-July to early-September summer break. November, February and March are the quietest and cheapest months, and the rain here is gentler than its reputation.

- From Germany, Switzerland and the Netherlands: 16 to 18 hours with one stop. Our guests from these countries tend to stay the longest, and a week or more makes the journey worthwhile. The shoulder months of April to June and September to October are ideal.

Our neighbourhood page has flight times, airport transfers and visa details.

### The truth about the rainy season

From November to March, Bali's wet season gets a bad name it does not entirely deserve, especially on the Bukit Peninsula, one of the drier parts of the island. Rain here usually arrives as a short, heavy downpour in the afternoon, and mornings are often bright and sunny.

- It stays warm. The sea and the pool are perfect for swimming all year.

- It is quiet. Fewer visitors, easier tables, emptier beaches.

- It is the best value of the year, apart from the Christmas and New Year rush.

- It is green. Gardens and bougainvillea are at their most lush.

At Nema, the compound is protected and calm in a storm. Swim in the warm pool, read on your balcony as the rain passes, and when it is time to move, practise under cover in the common area.

One date to check if you are coming in March: Nyepi, the Balinese Day of Silence, when the whole island, airport included, pauses for 24 hours. It is a remarkable experience, but plan around it.

### For retreat organisers

November to March is the ideal time to host a retreat at Nema. The whole property is easiest to reserve, rates are at their lowest outside Christmas and New Year, and the paved pool deck is cleared for practice, with the covered common area ready for rainy sessions. See our retreat page for details.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: When is the best time to visit Uluwatu?**

For sunshine without the crowds, come in April, May, June, September or October. The dry season runs roughly from April to October, but July and August are the busiest and most expensive months of the year.

**Q: Is it worth visiting Uluwatu in the rainy season?**

Yes, especially if you prefer quiet and value. From November to March, rain usually comes in short, heavy afternoon bursts rather than all day, mornings are often sunny, the sea and pools stay warm, and accommodation rates are at their lowest, apart from Christmas and New Year.

**Q: What is the quietest month in Uluwatu?**

The wet-season months from January to March are usually the quietest, apart from the Christmas and New Year period, which is busy across Bali.

**Q: Can you still do yoga in Uluwatu when it rains?**

Yes. At Nema, classes move from the paved pool deck to the covered common area when it rains, and the pool is still perfect for a swim.

**Q: When is Nyepi, the Balinese Day of Silence?**

Nyepi usually falls in March and its date changes every year. For 24 hours the whole island, including the airport, closes and guests stay within their accommodation. Check the date before you book a March trip.

Stay With Us

### Choose your season

Seasonal rates, always best direct. Message us with your dates and we will share the current rate for your dates.

# How to Run a Profitable Bali Retreat | Nema. Uluwatu
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/profitable-bali-retreat/
Summary: For retreat facilitators: off-season dates, avoiding school-holiday flight spikes, and using 10–20% partner dining discounts to protect your margin.

For Facilitators

## How to Run a More Profitable Retreat in Bali

Off-season dates, school-holiday flight traps and partner discounts.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 7 min read

Running a retreat in Bali is one of the most rewarding things a facilitator can do. It can also be one of the easiest ways to lose money, usually because of dates, not demand. Here is what we have learned from hosting groups at Nema.

### 1. Run it in the off-season

Accommodation is usually the largest fixed cost of a retreat. In Bali it is also the most seasonal. From November to March, Christmas and New Year aside, rates across the island are at their lowest, while what your participants are willing to pay for a week of practice, rest and community in Bali stays much the same.

That gap is your margin. Price your retreat on the value of the experience, not on your costs, and the off-season lets you keep more of every booking, or offer a more generous package at the same price.

The off-season is Bali's wet season, but on the Bukit Peninsula rain usually comes in short afternoon bursts. Plan the main practice for the morning, keep a covered space for backup, and the weather rarely gets in the way. Our guide to the best time to visit Uluwatu has the month-by-month detail.

### 2. Avoid the school-holiday flight trap

This is the mistake we see most often. A retreat sells out months ahead, then participants start pricing flights and discover the dates sit in school holidays. Fares jump, and cancellations follow.

Before you fix your dates, check the school calendars for the countries most of your participants fly from, and price a few return flights from your main cities. Watch in particular for:

- Australia: the long summer break from mid-December to late January, plus two-week breaks around April, July and late September to early October. Dates vary by state.

- United Kingdom: Christmas, February half-term, Easter, late May half-term, the summer holidays from late July to early September, and October half-term.

- Germany, the Netherlands and Switzerland: staggered summer holidays from July to September, plus Christmas, Easter and autumn breaks that vary by region.

- Christmas and New Year: the busiest and most expensive time to fly to Bali from almost everywhere.

Combine that with Bali's off-season and the strongest windows are usually November, early December, February and March. In March, also check the date of Nyepi, the Balinese Day of Silence, when the island and its airport close for 24 hours.

### 3. A simple margin example

The numbers below are illustrative only, to show how the levers work. They are not Nema's rates.

Illustrative retreat margin, peak versus off-season

| | Peak-season dates | Off-season dates

| Participants | 12 | 12

| Retreat price per person | 2,000 | 2,000

| Revenue | 24,000 | 24,000

| Accommodation | 9,000 | 6,500

| Teachers, food, transfers, extras | 8,000 | 8,000

| Your margin | 7,000 | 9,500

Same retreat, same price, same participants: moving the dates is often the single biggest lever on your profit. And off-season flights are usually cheaper too, which makes the retreat easier to sell and less likely to be cancelled.

### 4. Build margin into every line with partners

Retreat margins are thin, so every line of the budget counts. A venue with good local partnerships lets you include more in your package while keeping more of the price. At Nema:

- Partner restaurants, 10–20% off. Nema guests save 10–20% at partner restaurants such as YUKI, Kynd, Mood by Ours and Osteria Luna. Include a welcome dinner or closing feast in your package at the normal menu price, and the discount becomes your margin.

- Catering at Nema can be arranged on request, keeping the group together and the schedule simple.

- Fresh coconuts can be ordered in advance for your group: a low-cost, very Bali inclusion after morning practice that does not break the budget.

- Transport partners for airport transfers and excursions, so you are not negotiating rides for a group of twelve.

- A local itinerary. Using our local knowledge, we can help you design an agenda of local activities that works within your budget.

- Scooter rental is available for participants who want to explore in their free time.

- Drinks are available to buy on site, so you do not need to stock the property.

- Seating and custom mats: partners can supply extra seating for gatherings, and our custom mat partner can create co-branded yoga mats for your retreat.

Here is how a single partner dinner adds up. The numbers are illustrative only, not actual menu prices:

Illustrative partner dinner margin

| | Per guest | Group of 12

| Included in your package at menu price | 40 | 480

| What you pay with a 15% partner discount | 34 | 408

| Your margin on one dinner | 6 | 72

Do that for a welcome dinner, a closing dinner and a couple of lunches, and the partner discounts alone can add a meaningful amount to your margin, on top of the savings from off-season dates.

### 5. Your date-setting checklist

- List the three countries most of your participants will fly from.

- Rule out their school holidays, plus Christmas and New Year.

- Prefer November, early December, February or March, and check the Nyepi date.

- Price return flights from your main cities for your chosen week.

- Confirm the venue, then publish your dates six to nine months ahead.

When you are ready, see our retreat page or our venue checklist.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: When is the best time to run a retreat in Bali?**

For the best margin, run your retreat in Bali's off-season, from November to March, when accommodation is at its lowest price, and choose weeks outside the main school holidays of the countries your participants fly from. In practice that often means November, early December, February and March.

**Q: Why do retreat participants cancel?**

A common reason is the cost of flights. When retreat dates fall in or near school holidays, airfares can rise sharply, and participants who booked the retreat early may cancel once they price their flights. Checking fares from your main origin cities before you fix dates helps avoid this.

**Q: How can I make my Bali retreat more profitable?**

Lower your biggest fixed cost by choosing off-season dates, keep your price based on the value of the experience, and avoid school-holiday flight spikes. Then use your venue's partners: at Nema, partner restaurants give guests 10–20% off, so you can include group meals at menu price and keep the difference, and transport, catering, coconuts and activities can all be arranged through Nema's local partners.

**Q: What partner services does Nema offer retreat organisers?**

Nema works with many local partners: restaurants with 10–20% guest discounts, transport for airport transfers and excursions, catering at Nema, coconuts ordered in advance for the group, extra seating, custom co-branded yoga mats, and scooter rental. The team can also help design an itinerary of local activities to fit your budget, and drinks are available to buy on site.

**Q: How many participants can a retreat at Nema hold?**

Nema has 12 private studios with one queen bed each: 12 participants in private rooms, or up to 24 sharing. Classes run on the paved pool deck, which staff clear of furniture, or in the covered common area when it rains.

# Learn to Surf at Thomas Beach, Uluwatu | Nema.
URL: https://nemauluwatu.com/journal/learn-to-surf-thomas-beach/
Summary: How to learn to surf at Thomas Beach in Uluwatu, Bali: the wave, the best tides and season, booking a lesson, safety on the reef, and a simple beginner plan.

Surf

## Learn to Surf at Thomas Beach, Uluwatu

Uluwatu's friendliest learner wave, a short walk from your studio.

By the Nema. Uluwatu team · 23 October 2026 · Updated 25 October 2026 · 7 min read

Uluwatu is famous for world-class reef breaks that most people should only watch from the cliffs. But a short walk from Nema, Thomas Beach has one of the area's friendliest waves for learning: softer, quieter and usually uncrowded. Here is how to learn to surf there, safely and without wasting a morning.

### The wave at Thomas Beach

Thomas Beach sits on the Bukit Peninsula's west coast, just south of Padang Padang, towards Uluwatu. It is a reef break with lefts and rights, and on small to medium swells, around head high and below, the waves are soft and playful with a relatively easy paddle out. It is a place to practise fundamentals rather than chase long rides, which is exactly what you want when you are learning.

It is also quiet. The walk down from the cliff, with steps at the end, keeps the crowds away, so you spend more time catching waves and less time dodging other surfers.

Because it breaks over reef rather than sand, Thomas Beach is not a place to teach yourself. Learn with an instructor who knows the currents and can choose the right tide.

### When to go: season, tide and time of day

- Season: the dry season, roughly April to October, brings south-east trade winds that blow offshore on Uluwatu's west-facing breaks, so waves are cleaner and more consistent. It is the best time to learn here.

- Wet season: from November to March the wind is often onshore on this coast and currents can be stronger. Good instructors simply move beginners to the east side of the Bukit on those days.

- Tide: mid to high tide. At low tide the reef is exposed and too shallow to surf safely.

- Swell: small to medium. On bigger swells, a strong current can build from the sets breaking towards Uluwatu, and it is no longer a beginner wave.

- Time of day: early mornings are usually the calmest and least crowded, and you are back at the pool before the heat of the day.

### Booking a lesson

Plenty of surf schools work around Padang Padang, Thomas Beach and Dreamland, and most will pick the best beginner spot for the day's conditions. As a rough guide in 2026:

Indicative surf lesson prices in Uluwatu

| Lesson | Typical length | Indicative price

| Small-group beginner lesson | 2 hours | From about IDR 400,000 (US$25–35)

| Private lesson | 2 hours | About IDR 650,000–700,000

| Board rental | Half day or day | Ask locally; prices vary by board

Prices change, so confirm what is included: usually a soft-top board, a rash vest and a safety briefing, and sometimes transport to the break. Our front desk can recommend local instructors and help you book.

### Reef safety and etiquette

- Never surf alone as a beginner. Most Bali breaks have no lifeguards.

- Wear reef booties if you are not confident, and fall flat and shallow rather than diving.

- Respect the tide. If the reef is showing, the session is over.

- Watch the current. If you feel it pulling, paddle across it, not against it, and signal your instructor.

- Sun: a rash vest and reef-safe sunscreen; the equatorial sun is strong even on cloudy days.

- Etiquette: do not drop in on someone already riding a wave, keep out of the way of surfers paddling back out, and be friendly to locals in the lineup.

### A simple three-day beginner plan

- Day 1: a two-hour lesson on a soft-top board: paddling, popping up and reading the whitewater. Afternoon by the pool.

- Day 2: a second lesson at the best spot for the swell, aiming to catch green, unbroken waves with your instructor.

- Day 3: a supervised session or private lesson at Thomas Beach on a mid-to-high tide, then sunset at Single Fin to watch the experts on the main Uluwatu break.

Three mornings will not make you a surfer, but most people are standing and riding by the end of them, and hooked for life.

### Surf for groups and retreats

Morning surf, afternoon yoga is one of the great Bali retreat formats, and Thomas Beach is on Nema's doorstep. For groups, we can help arrange lessons with local instructors, transport to other breaks when conditions change, and coconuts waiting when everyone gets back. See our retreat page or group stays.

Other beginner-friendly options nearby include Baby Padang (at mid to high tide) and Dreamland's sandy beach break, about 20 minutes away. Our guide to the best time to visit Uluwatu covers the seasons in more detail.

Quick Answers

### Good to Know

**Q: Is Thomas Beach good for beginner surfers?**

Yes, on the right day. Thomas Beach is a reef break with soft, playful waves on small to medium swells at mid to high tide, and it is usually uncrowded. Because it breaks over reef, beginners should learn there with an instructor who knows the tides and currents.

**Q: What is the best time to learn to surf in Uluwatu?**

The dry season, roughly April to October, brings south-east trade winds that blow offshore on Uluwatu's west-facing breaks, giving the cleanest, most consistent waves. Early mornings are usually the calmest. In the wet season, from November to March, winds are often onshore on this coast, and instructors may take beginners to breaks on the east side of the Bukit instead.

**Q: What tide is best for surfing Thomas Beach?**

Mid to high tide. At low tide the reef becomes exposed and the water is too shallow for safe surfing. Check a tide chart, or let your instructor time the session.

**Q: How much does a surf lesson cost in Uluwatu?**

As a rough guide, small-group beginner lessons in the Uluwatu area start at around IDR 400,000 (about US$25–35) for two hours, and private lessons are around IDR 650,000–700,000. Prices usually include a board and rash vest; check what is included when you book.

**Q: How far is Thomas Beach from Nema Uluwatu?**

Thomas Beach is a short walk from Nema down a local pathway, with steps down to the sand. Our front desk can recommend local instructors and help arrange a lesson.
